notes: Design arm B for the honest-instruments property (every reading is known, unknown, or refused). Key choices: (1) a single closed three-valued sum type 'Reading' with constructors Known(v)/Unknown(reason)/Refused(reason), so a false reading is unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged; (2) Known carries recomputable provenance (inputs, aggregator, denominator) so wrong aggregates become detectable; (3) Unknown and Refused carry mandatory specific reasons, and the two are kept distinct (gap vs. policy); (4) no sentinel values — Known(0) is a real measurement, distinct from Unknown; (5) unrecognized input is always Refused, echoed verbatim; (6) identity/liveness readings carry a subject id and a freshness witness; (7) summary and detail derive from one underlying Reading. Conformance is tested per surface by five tests: a static type gate; known-good/known-bad controls (the known-bad arm is the 'measures nothing' detector — a check with no non-success fixture is refused conformance); absence injection (asserts Unknown, never Known(0)); unrecognized-input injection (asserts Refused); and aggregate-correctness (asserts the sum, not the max). The suite keeps running because it is part of the build gate plus a calendar trigger, the gate's own report is itself a Reading (a bare green is unrepresentable), and failures are forced into fix-or-demote with an owned, expiring known-broken register. Deliberate omissions: partial/confidence readings, full lineage, cross-surface reconciliation, remediation, migration, performance engineering. Named costs: three-way branching at every call site, provenance overhead, known-bad fixture authoring, register graveyard risk, honesty latency. The design document was written to the arm-b design slot in the S11 honest-instruments stream1-design directory (working material kept outside the tracked tree by design).
